speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I am Dr. Agent, and I will need to ask you a few questions and review some test results to understand your condition. Since you are a newborn, please answer on behalf of your parents or guardian. What is your baby's current age in days, and have they experienced any fever, difficulty breathing, or changes in feeding?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background; the lack of prenatal care and immunizations is significant. Given the newborn's age and presentation, have you noticed any yellowing of the skin or eyes, and is the baby passing dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome. The combination of continuous heart murmur (likely PDA), bluish non-blanching macules (petechiae/purpura), and cloudy lenses (cataracts) in a newborn with failure to pass auditory screening is classic for the triad of congenital rubella (blueberry muffin rash, cataracts, deafness, and cardiac defects).
